anomaly_signals.detail: 60 errors out of 407 spans — 14.7% error rate on the payments DB. Primary driver of the db_incident scenario, likely causing cascading failures upstream.
36 errors out of 407 spans — 8.8% error rate. Directly downstream of postgres-payments degradation; failing queries are propagating to the payments service layer.
23 errors out of 537 spans (4.3% error rate) plus 25 genai_tool_failures cluster here. Tools are failing at an elevated rate, likely impacting agent task completion.
34 token truncation events recorded across 863 spans (~3.9% truncation rate). Responses may be incomplete, causing downstream agent/workflow logic errors.
p99 latency of 11,777.8 ms across the stack is significantly elevated. LLM inference latency is a prime contributor given its high span count (863) and known susceptibility to tail latency spikes.
9 errors out of 520 spans (1.7% error rate). Likely a secondary effect of tool-executor failures and LLM truncations degrading agent task execution.

recommended_action: Immediately investigate postgres-payments: check for connection pool exhaustion, slow queries, or disk/IO saturation driving the 14.7% DB error rate and cascading failures into payments-service. In parallel, review tool-executor logs for the 25 GenAI tool failures and audit LLM context window sizing to address 34 token truncations. Consider circuit-breaking payments-service from postgres-payments to limit blast radius while the DB incident is remediated.
summary: A confirmed db_incident is centred on postgres-payments (14.7% error rate), cascading failures into payments-service (8.8%) and contributing to an elevated system-wide p99 latency of ~11.8 s. Compounding issues include 25 GenAI tool failures in tool-executor and 34 LLM token truncations in llm-gemini, suggesting the agent/workflow layer is also degraded independently of the DB incident.
